% note: Role: confirmatory settings are those a test uses at that shape; a five-test setting is a setting of the confirmatory run (the file's own list) that no test uses at that shape; the rest are exploratory. Haiku-medium enters Tests~1--3 as a vote of $k$ samples; the row here is its single sample, and the votes are in the Study~1 test tables.
% note: Samples per puzzle is the stamped samples divided by the stamped puzzles. Step voting has no designed number of calls, so its samples-per-puzzle cell is a dash; it made 1,086 calls.
% note: Refusals and truncations: 0 in every row; the one exception is step voting's refusal count, which its row does not stamp (the file stamps all 1,086 of its calls as answered, with no refusal category).
% note: Cost per sample: for the Haiku settings, one sample's mean list cost (a vote of $k$ samples costs $k$ times this); for step voting, all its calls on a puzzle; for Opus and Sonnet, their one answer. The Batch column is the same at the Batch price (half the list price). Cost per correct answer is the total cost of one sample per puzzle over the expected number of those samples that are right, at list price. Costs are in US dollars.
% note: Interval type: the Haiku settings' and step voting's accuracy intervals are cluster bootstraps over puzzles; the one-sample Opus and Sonnet settings' are Clopper--Pearson intervals, which are exact: they come from the binomial distribution itself, with no resampling.
